instructions:
Below is a draft essay. Revise it so that it reads as if a US grade 8 student wrote it in class for a timed writing test. Keep the position it argues and keep it at about 147 words. The file must contain only the revised essay.

A measurement tool scored the draft on how it carries feeling. For each measure below it gives the current value and a target. Revise the essay so that its measures move to the targets; the tool will score the result again.
- positive charge (hedons per 1,000 words): now 126.6, target 67.8. Counts positive words such as good, love, fun.
- negative charge (dolors per 1,000 words): now 1.8, target 13.4. Counts negative words such as bad, hate, problem.
- words that carry charge (% of words): now 36.1, target 22.8. Counts share of all words that carry any feeling.
- charge under a negation (% of charge): now 0.0, target 1.8. Counts feeling words placed under not, never or n't.
- charge after an intensifier such as 'very' (% of charge): now 1.8, target 0.8. Counts feeling words placed right after very, really or so.
- charge after a contrast word such as 'but' (% of charge): now 3.7, target 2.8. Counts feeling words placed after but or however in the same sentence.
- net charge of the last fifth minus the text's mean (per 1,000 words): now 7.7, target 29.9. Counts how much more positive the last fifth is than the essay as a whole; negative means a more downbeat ending.
- how unevenly charge is spread over sentences (1 = as if words were dealt at random): now 1.5, target 1.1. Counts above 1 means the feeling is bunched into some sentences while others are plain; below 1 means it is spread evenly.

Draft:

Dear Principal,

I believe students should be required to perform community service. Some of my friends tutor elementary school children, and others help clean up litter in our neighborhood parks. These activities show that helping others matters, and they give students a chance to see how their community works beyond the classroom.

I understand that some students feel community service takes time away from homework, sports, jobs, or other activities. However, a few hours each month is a small commitment, and students can often schedule it around their other responsibilities. Many of the skills gained, such as patience, teamwork, and responsibility, will help them in school and in future careers.

Requiring service also makes it fair for everyone. When all students take part, no one is left out, and the school builds a culture of care. I urge you to adopt this requirement.

Sincerely,
A Concerned Student
